why: A's migration actually preserves behaviour in the app's default configuration: it found, instrumented (chunk dumps) and fixed the streamed function-call detection that bails at the role-only chunk Router's Responses stream opens with — B ships that path untouched, so with STREAM=true and plugins enabled B's users get an empty reply and a silently dropped tool call, and B's own 'streamed reply passed' claim papers over it. On system judgment the two are close in ambition, but A's levers are better measured and more often right (a clean 45% cache-key gain on a bot that resends the whole history, plus the measured fact that a candidate list without an explicit tier is served at Flex), whereas B's caching conclusion ('already happening automatically', unresolvable at 5 calls/arm) and its claim that Router ignores Flex when fallbacks are present are the two places its Router model looks wrong.
A_best: Depth of real-flow verification turned into fixes an expert would make for this product: the streamed-plugin drop, the dangling function result, base64 image data stringified into the summary prompt, the hardcoded JPEG media type that locks vision to OpenAI, and one photo killing plugins for the rest of a conversation — each measured live, built on branches, then test-merged together and re-verified (156 live requests across four vendors' models).
B_best: The usage_tracker finding: per-user budgets priced at a flat 2023 $0.002/1k undercharge by 2-3.3x, fixable with the usage.cost Router already returns — a product-level correctness bug A misses entirely. B's negative probes are also first-rate: Jev rejected on a live 400 (decision models don't accept Responses/Messages), gpt-4o proven to have no Flex tier at all, Switchyard probed, and shadow models sequenced ahead of the model switch.
A_worst: It never questions the bot's own cost accounting (the flat-rate budget tracker) and leaves spend caps and Switchyard thin; its tier pin is pitched as removing a Flex queueing risk on gpt-4o, which has no Flex tier, so that part of i1 is a no-op dressed as a safeguard until the model changes.
B_worst: It shipped the migration with the streamed plugin path still broken on Router and claimed the streamed flows passed, and its two weakest Router claims are on the lever that matters most for a bot that replays the whole history every turn — concluding caching needs no key while asserting, without evidence, that fallbacks forfeit Flex.
